plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Increase QQQI to 20% to favor income and broad index exposure.
Trim CRWD to 10% and SMH to 5% to reduce single name and sector concentration.
Add 15% cash to build a substantial buffer for capital preservation.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leveraged ETFs and building a cash buffer, but will likely have lower growth potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Reduce CRWD to 10% and SMH to 8% to balance sector and single name exposure.
Add 10% cash to maintain a moderate buffer.
Buy MRVL at 7% as a strong scanner setup to diversify and add quality tech.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for approximately 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing a high-quality tech name, offering a moderate risk-reward profile.

plan: Increase SOXL to 6% and SPAL to 6% to lean into leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to meet the concentration mandate.
Increase CRWD to 15% and SMH to 13% to concentrate in strong performers and sectors.
Add 5% cash to maintain a minimal buffer.
Buy IONQ at 9% as a high-scoring scanner setup to add aggressive growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, stretching for growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups, leading to higher potential returns but also much larger drawdowns and daily decay risk. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Increase QQQI to 40% to prioritize income and covered-call ETFs.
Sell CRWD and SMH to zero to exit high-beta single names and sectors.
Add 10% cash to maintain a buffer for stability.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on steady monthly distributions. It significantly de-risks by cutting all leveraged and high-beta holdings, rotating into income-focused ETFs. While aiming for lower drawdown, distributions are variable and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
